title: Framing Political Bias in Multilingual LLMs Across Pakistani Languages

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating ideological stance using a culturally adapted Political Compass Test (PCT) mapped to economic and social axes, and conducting a multi-level framing analysis (frame dimensions, named entity recognition, and sentiment polarity) on model-generated news headlines across 11 socio-political topics.

Comparing the political stance and framing strategies of LLMs when prompted in English versus five low-resource Pakistani languages (Urdu, Punjabi, Sindhi, Pashto, and Balochi) to observe systematic language-conditioned ideological shifts.

Analyzing how models align with or mischaracterize culturally specific sociopolitical contexts in Pakistan by translating and adapting Western political taxonomies to regional topics and measuring framing variations.
